swanhanger.claim: Saniger is a worn-down form of SWANHANGER, and the older spelling is on record for five hundred years.
swanhanger.proof: One deed, catalogued twice. Berkeley Castle holds it as BCM/A/1/24/185, 11 April 51 Edw. III (1377), 'Elias de Swonhongre and William Panyter'. Birmingham Archives holds a copy as MS 3549/20, same day, same parties, and calls the land 'a messuage, land and appurtenances in SWANHANGER, co. Glouc.'
swanhanger.gloss: Gloucestershire Archives settles it outright in D654/III/9: 'Messuage called Oldminsters in SWANHANGER ... [Saniger in Hinton]'. The archivist supplied the modern name in brackets.

swanhanger.people: Three forenames carry the older spelling: Thomas de Swonhungre (24 entries), John (10) and William (8) — a family that had already taken its name from the place by about 1300, five centuries before anyone in this archive was born.
swanhanger.field: Thomas de Swonhungre granted land in WESTFELD in the early 14th century (BCM/A/1/65/18). John Saniger released three acres in WESTFIELD, Saniger, in 1601. Edward Saniger exchanged three-quarters of an acre in WESTFIELD in 1716. One field, four hundred years, three spellings of one name.

estate.reading: In 1692 Edward Saniger is a CLOTHIER. In 1709 the same man at the same address is a GENT. Bigland, writing later, calls him 'Edward Saniger of Saniger, Gent.' and records his wife Esther's death in June 1693. The deeds show the promotion; the gravestone shows the household it happened to.

neighbours.note: Bigland's Berkeley monuments name six more households as 'of Saniger'. None of them is called Saniger. A hamlet, not a family seat.

hinton: Bigland describes the tithing in 1791: “4. Hinton, wherein are Wanswell, a reputed Manor … SANIGER, long held by an old Family of the same Name, in which also is another Estate belonging to WOODWARD: Hinton, Halmore; and Breadstone.” The Woodward estate is not a guess — Daniel Woodward of Bristol, wine merchant, leased Panthurst in Saniger in 1749, and the deed is D2957/41/58.

minchinhampton: Bigland found a second family under the -gear spelling twenty miles away, at Minchinhampton: Mary, daughter of William Sanigear, d. 24 Feb 1759; William their son, d. 14 July 1760; and Sarah, wife of [William] Sanigear and daughter of Thomas and Ann Lawton, d. 14 June 1770, aged 34.
